newsitem.title: INDIA: Three followers of Dalai Lama murdered in India.
newsitem.headline: Three followers of Dalai Lama murdered in India.

text.p: Three disciples of Tibet's god-king the Dalai Lama have been murdered in the northern Indian town of Dharamsala, a spokesman for the exiled Tibetan spiritual leader said on Thursday.
T.C. Tethong, the Dalai Lama's representative in the Indian capital, said Ven Lobsang Gyatso, the head of a Buddhist school, was found stabbed to death in his residence on Tuesday evening.

Two of his students, Lobsang Ngawang and Ngawang Lodroe, were found severely injured and died while being taken to hospital, he said. The nature of their injuries and their whereabouts when found were not disclosed.
"No motive has been established and the murder of these three persons is tragic and a loss to the Tibetan community," Tethong said in a statment.
A state police official in Dharamsala said six suspects had been detained.
Gyatso, who was close to the Dalai Lama, was a staunch critic of Shugden Dorjie, considered by some Tibetans to be a deity.
Last year the Dalai Lama publicly asked Tibetans to stop worshipping Shugden on the grounds he was not a god but a spirit, Jampal Chosang, an official in the Dalai Lama's Delhi office, told Reuters.
Gyatso's Buddhist School of Dialectics teaches Buddhist scholars who follow the Dalai Lama's orthodoxy, Jampal said.
The Dalai Lama has been based in Dharamsala in the northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh since he fled there in 1959 following a failed anti-Chinese uprising.

The Dalai Lama, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent campaign to win autonomy for his homeland, says he wants self-government and freedom of worship in the deeply religious Buddhist region.
More than 100,000 Tibetan exiles now live in India, forming the backbone of the Dalai Lama's non-violent movement.
